fields.aka: Bhaktikevala Audulomi, Bhakti Keval Audulomi, Pramoda Bihārī Guha Ṭhākurtā, Patitapāvana dāsa Brahmacārī
fields.place: Born at Bānāripāḍā (Barisal); Śrī Caitanya Maṭha, Māyāpura; Gauḍīya Mission, Calcutta
fields.notes: Son of Śaratcandra Guha Ṭhākurtā and Bhuvanamohinī; brother of Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī. Dīkṣā as Patitapāvana dāsa, sannyāsa from Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī. Led the Navadvīpa parikramā and Śrī Caitanya Maṭha 1940-47 for Bhakti Prasāda Purī; president-ācārya of the Gauḍīya Mission from 16 February 1954; began the yearly Vraja-maṇḍala parikramā (1957-60).

fields.aka: Saranga Gosvāmī Mahārāja, Śrīla Bhakti Sharanga Gosvāmī, Bhakti Saranga Gosvāmī, Atulacandra Bandyopādhyāya, Atulacandra Gosvāmī
fields.place: London (1933-37); Śrī Gauḍīya Saṅgha: Māyāpura (samādhi; Gaura-Nityānanda temple at Nandana Ācārya's house) and Imli-talā, Vṛndāvana (puṣpa-samādhi)
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Sarasvatī (dīkṣā), Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣaka Śrīdhara Deva Gosvāmī (sannyāsa)
fields.works: About twenty books; editor of the weekly Gauḍīya; the English Sajjana-toṣaṇī; articles in The Harmonist
fields.notes: Atulacandra, of the family of Nityānanda Prabhu, a high government official who left everything for the mission of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī; preached in London (met the King and Queen, World Congress of Faiths at Oxford, 1937) and initiated disciples there in his guru's lifetime. The first to take sannyāsa from Bhakti Rakṣaka Śrīdhara Mahārāja; founded the Śrī Gauḍīya Saṅgha, recovered Imli-talā in Vṛndāvana.

fields.aka: Bhakti Pradip Tīrtha, Pradip Thirta Majaraj, Jagadīśa Vasu, Bhakti Pradīpa Tīrtha Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.disappearance: Agrahāyaṇa Pūrṇimā (Gauḍīya calendar), Bengali 1360 (December 1953), at the Puruṣottama Maṭha, Purī
fields.place: Born at Sandvīpa-Hātiyā (Noākhālī); Godruma; East Bengal and Orissa; Europe (1933); Puruṣottama Maṭha, Purī
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura (dīkṣā), Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Sarasvatī (sannyāsa, 1920)
fields.works: Articles and English translations (a life of Śrī Caitanya, the Bhagavad-gītā); books in Bengali and English
fields.notes: Jagadīśa, son of Rajanīkānta Vasu and Bidhumukhī, elder brother of Bhakti Prasāda Purī (Ananta Vāsudeva). Met Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura at Māyāpura on Gaura Pūrṇimā 1910 and took dīkṣā from him at Godruma; the first sannyāsī of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (Kārtika 1920). Preached in Europe from 1933; president of the Gauḍīya Mission from 1941; left his body at Purī listening to the Caitanya-bhāgavata.

fields.aka: Ananta Vāsudeva, Bhakti Prasād Purī, Vāsudeva Prabhu, Ananta Vāsudeva Paravidyābhūṣaṇa
fields.appearance: Bhādra Śukla Ṣaṣṭhī 1302 (25 August 1895), at Sandvīpa-Hātiyā (Noākhālī)
fields.disappearance: 8 March 1958, at Vṛndāvana (kuñja of Śrī Rādhāramaṇa)
fields.place: Born at Sandvīpa-Hātiyā (Noākhālī); Calcutta (Bhāgavata Press, Gauḍīya Maṭha); Māyāpura (Yogapīṭha); Gayā (sannyāsa); Vṛndāvana
fields.notes: Ananta, son of Rajanīkānta Vasu and Bidhumukhī, younger brother of Bhakti Pradīpa Tīrtha. Dīkṣā in 1918 as Ananta Vāsudeva Brahmacārī; wrote down his guru's commentaries, ran the Bhāgavata Press, began the Vyāsa-pūjā and composed the praṇāma-mantras of the guru-varga (1929). Elected ācārya of the Gauḍīya Maṭha and Mission in 1937; sannyāsa at Gayā in 1939 as Bhakti Prasāda Purī; in 1954 made Bhakti Kevala Auḍulomi ācārya and retired to Vṛndāvana.

fields.aka: Bhakti Pramod Purī, Promode Purī Gosvāmī, Śrīla Bhakti Pramoda Purī Gosvāmī Mahārāja, Pramoda Bhūṣaṇa (birth name), Pranavananda Brahmacārī
fields.appearance: Āśvina Śukla Caturthī (Gauḍīya calendar); 8 October 1898, at Gaṅgānandapura (Jessore)
fields.disappearance: Kārtika Śukla Caturdaśī (Gauḍīya calendar); 22 November 1999, 2:07 am, at the age of 101
fields.guru: Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura (dīkṣā on Janmāṣṭamī 1923 at the Ultadanga Gauḍīya Maṭha); sannyāsa from Bhakti Gaurava Vaikhānasa Mahārāja (1947; another text: 1942)
fields.notes: Pramoda Bhūṣaṇa Cakravartī of Gaṅgānandapura (Jessore); B.Sc. in chemistry (Bangabasi College); met Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī while working at the Post Commission in Calcutta; dīkṣā on Janmāṣṭamī 1923; editor of the Gauḍīya Maṭha's publications. Took sannyāsa from his godbrother Vaikhānasa Mahārāja at Cāṁpāhāṭi by his guru's order in a dream. Very affectionate to Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja. Lived to 101.

fields.aka: Kṛṣṇa dāsa bābājī, Kṛṣṇadāsa Bābājī, Prabhupāda's Godbrother Akiñcana Kṛṣṇadās Bābājī Mahārāj
fields.disappearance: Vaiśākha Kṛṣṇa Pañcamī (Gauḍīya calendar); samādhi at Nandagrāma
fields.place: East Bengal (born); Navadvīpa / Māyāpura (winter); Vṛndāvana (Bon Mahārāja's bhajana-kuṭīra); samādhi at Nandagrāma
fields.notes: Called akiñcana and paramahaṁsa by A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda. Chanted Hare Kṛṣṇa day and night with his guru's blessing; famous kīrtana leader, answered everything with a laughing «Hare Kṛṣṇa!». Had no disciples, built nothing, criticised no one. Sang kīrtana at A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī's sannyāsa (Mathurā, 1959).

fields.aka: Bhakti Vilās Tīrtha, Kuñjabihārī Vidyābhūṣaṇa, Kunjabihari Vidyābhūṣaṇa bābājī, Kuñja-dā, Kuñja Vihārī Dāsa
fields.place: Calcutta; Śrī Caitanya Maṭha and the Yogapīṭha, Māyāpura
fields.notes: Kuñjabihārī Vidyābhūṣaṇa («Kuñja-dā»), a post-office employee who gave his earnings to the maṭha; manager of the Gauḍīya Maṭha from its beginning and Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī's right hand in building the maṭhas; helped carry Gaura Kiśora dāsa Bābājī's body. After 1937 ācārya of Śrī Caitanya Maṭha, Māyāpura (the mission split between him and Ananta Vāsudeva). Grieved his guru by doing his mother's śrāddha by the smārta rules (1934).

fields.appearance: Pauṣa Kṛṣṇa Navamī (Gauḍīya calendar); 23 December 1921 (another text: 1916), at Piljaṅgā (Khulna)

fields.guru: Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Sarasvatī (dīkṣā, c. 1929); later re-initiated by Kanupriya Gosvāmī of Navadvīpa
fields.notes: Gṛhastha disciple of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī, who called him his right hand (Ananta Vāsudeva the other) and «Vyāsa»; editor of the Gauḍīya, later secretary of the Gauḍīya Mission; was to complete the Vaiṣṇava-mañjuṣā encyclopedia. Long after his guru's departure he disagreed about the Madhva line and took initiation again from Kanupriya Gosvāmī in Vṛndāvana.
